metadata.theme: Curiosity with care, reading clues closely, and respecting the past
metadata.premise: Sami Kade leads a small archaeology team into a sealed tomb in the desert ruins of Ameru, where the carved walls warn that the sleeper in the stone box must not be woken.

items.name: Soft brush
items.description: A brush with a long handle. It clears dust from old carvings without scratching them.

clues.name: Tapping card
clues.description: A clay card from the dirt. It shows a hand that taps the door three times.

clues.name: The low note
clues.description: A carved song that ends on the lowest note. It was hidden under grey dust.

passages.title: Dawn at Ameru
paragraphs: The sun rose over the dry hills of Ameru. Sami Kade stood at the edge of the old city.
Sami was an archaeologist. That means Sami studies the ancient past and keeps it safe.
Ren hugged a notebook. Hollis sat on the cart and ate a long, dry biscuit.
"Why did the sand cross the river?" asked Hollis. "To reach the other bank!" Nobody laughed. Hollis grinned anyway.
Yesterday, Ren found a sealed door under the dirt. Today, the team would open it.

choices.label: Help Hollis unload the cart
Look at Ren's map first

passages.title: The Cart
paragraphs: Hollis filled a small tank with water from the cart. Sami hunted through a crate for the brush.
Inside lay ropes, lamps and a soft brush. The brush had a long wooden handle.
"Take it," said Hollis. "A brush is better than a hammer. Old things need a gentle touch."
Sami tucked the brush into a belt. Then Sami looked at the dark hill and its door.

choices.label: Ask Ren about the map
Walk to the door

passages.title: Ren's Map
paragraphs: Ren spread the map on a flat rock. A small clay card lay beside it.
"I hunted in the dirt and found this card," said Ren. "Look. It shows a hand that tapped the door."
The card showed three taps, then a push. Under the hand was a tiny carved line: slow, slow, slow.
"The old builders wanted us to knock first," said Sami. "I think they were polite."
Ren wrote in the notebook: Tap three times. Do not push.

choices.label: Walk to the door with the card
Help Ren copy the picture first

passages.title: Copying the Picture
paragraphs: Ren copied the tapping picture into the notebook, line by line.
Sami waited, patient and calm, while the pencil scratched on the page.
"Good notes last longer than memory," said Sami.
Ren tucked the notebook away.
Hollis yawned. "We could always come back tomorrow," he said.

choices.label: Walk to the door with the card
Decide to come back another day instead

passages.title: The Sealed Door
paragraphs: The team walked down a stair cut into the rock. It was dark and cool.
At the bottom stood the door. A tall Keeper was carved on it, one hand held flat.
The Keeper looked kind but firm. It seemed to say: slow down.
Hollis tapped his foot. "A door is a door," he said. "Let us just shove it."

choices.label: Tap the stone three times, as the card shows
choices.lockedHint: Is there a card that shows how to knock?

choices.label: Push the door with both hands

passages.title: Tap, Tap, Tap
paragraphs: Sami tapped the stone once. Then twice. Then three times.
Deep inside the rock, something clicked. The door began to sink into the floor without a sound.
"Well done, Ren," said Sami. "Your card paid off."
A cool breath of air drifted out. The first chamber lay ahead.

choices.label: Step inside
Wait for your eyes to adjust to the dark

passages.title: Eyes in the Dark
paragraphs: They stood still and let their eyes adjust to the dark.
Slowly, shapes formed: a wide floor, far walls, and carved lines.
"Better to see first," said Sami. "Now we are ready."
Ren rubbed tired eyes. "We could stop here for today," said Ren.

choices.label: Step inside
Decide the day has been long enough

passages.title: The Groaning Door
paragraphs: Sami and Hollis pushed. The door groaned and shook. Dust rained down.
Slowly it slid open. Everyone coughed and waved the dust away.
"Next time," said Sami, "we knock first." Ren made a note of that.
The door was open. Nothing was broken. The first chamber waited.

choices.label: Step inside
Check the Keeper's carving for cracks

passages.title: A Careful Look
paragraphs: Sami looked over the carved Keeper on the stone door.
Its stone face had no new cracks, only old dust.
"We got lucky," said Sami. "Carvings this old can break fast."
Hollis brushed dust from his shirt. "Maybe that's enough excitement for one day," he said.

choices.label: Step inside
Agree this is a good place to stop for today

passages.title: The Hall of Sand
paragraphs: The first chamber was wide and quiet. Pale tiles and dark tiles covered the floor.
A Keeper was carved on the wall. Its carved feet stood only on the pale tiles.
Above it ran a line of pictures. A bird flew far off. A walker crossed the sand with soft steps.
Ren read the pictures aloud. "Walk soft," said Ren. "Only on the pale ones, I think."

choices.label: Step only on the pale tiles
Hop across the dark tiles to save time

passages.title: A Slippery Floor
paragraphs: A dark tile tipped under Hollis. A bank of sand slid out like water.
Hollis felt his boots sink. He sat down in the dirt with a bump. He was not hurt, only very dusty.
Sami dusted off his hat. "The tiles told us," said Sami. "We should have read them."
The sand settled, and everyone stood on the pale tiles to catch a breath.

choices.label: Go on to the next chamber
Look at the tile that tipped, before moving on

passages.title: The Hidden Bird
paragraphs: Ren bent down and looked at the tile that had tipped.
Under the dust lay a tiny carved bird. It pointed at the pale path.
"The hall was trying to help us," said Ren. "We just walked too fast."
Hollis rubbed his dusty knee. "That was enough of a tumble for me today," he said.

choices.label: Go on to the next chamber
Suggest resting here for the rest of today

passages.title: The Hall of Water
paragraphs: The second chamber held a round cistern, deep and dry. It looked like a huge stone tank.
A ladder with one missing rung led to a ledge on the far side.
A Keeper was carved here too. Its head was tilted, as if it was listening.
The carving was covered in grey dust. Some of the pictures were hard to see.

choices.label: Dust the carving with the soft brush
choices.lockedHint: A soft brush from the cart would clear this dust.

choices.label: Cross by the ladder and keep going

passages.title: Under the Dust
paragraphs: Sami dusted the wall with slow, soft strokes. The grey cloud drifted away.
A song was carved beneath the Keeper. Music notes ran from high to low.
"A long, low note," said Ren. "It ends on the lowest one. Write it down."
Sami smiled. "A careful look gives us a gift," said Sami.
They climbed the ladder, one rung at a time, toward the ledge above.

choices.label: Walk on to the third chamber
Rest a moment on the ledge first

passages.title: Resting on the Ledge
paragraphs: They rested on the ledge and drank a little water.
Hollis hummed a slow tune, low and long.
"That is almost the note from the wall," said Ren, smiling.
Sami laughed softly. "Save your voice. We may need it soon."
Sami looked at the new clue. "That might be a good place to stop," said Sami.

choices.label: Walk on to the third chamber
Decide the clue is enough for one day

passages.title: Over the Ladder
paragraphs: The team climbed the ladder and rested on the ledge. Hollis hummed a tune.
Ren looked back at the dusty carving. "I wonder what it said," said Ren.
Sami lifted a lamp. "We will not find out now. Come on."
Ahead, a wide arch led to the third chamber.

choices.label: Walk on to the third chamber
Ask Hollis what he thinks they missed

passages.title: What Hollis Thinks
paragraphs: "We might have missed a clue," said Hollis, looking back.
"But old things keep their secrets," said Sami. "We walked on, and so should we."
Ren nodded, a little sad, and followed without a word.
Ren sighed. "Maybe we should come back when we are less tired," said Ren.

choices.label: Walk on to the third chamber
Decide to turn back and try again another day

passages.title: The Hall of Song
paragraphs: The third chamber was round, with a bronze horn set in the wall.
A Keeper was carved beside it, with its mouth open as if to sing.
The next door was shut tight. Where the lock should be, there was a round hole.
The hole looked like the open end of the horn. Sami tapped the wall. It rang like a bell.

choices.label: Hum the low note into the hole
choices.lockedHint: The dust on the water wall hid a song.

choices.label: Blow the big horn as hard as you can

passages.title: One Low Note
paragraphs: Ren took a breath and began to sing the long, low note. It was small, but it was true.
The hole hummed back. The shut door slid aside, soft as a sigh.
Hollis clapped. "I can sing too," he said. Sami raised one eyebrow.
Past the door, the passage bent toward a place that smelled of old smoke.

choices.label: Walk on
Look back at the Keeper before walking on

passages.title: A New Look
paragraphs: Ren glanced back at the carved Keeper before walking on.
Its stone mouth seemed to curve, almost like a smile.
"Maybe it likes a good listener," said Ren.
Hollis yawned. "Maybe we should call it a day," he said.

choices.label: Walk on
Decide to stop here for today

passages.title: The Big Blow
paragraphs: Hollis pressed his lips to the horn and blew. A huge, rough bark filled the hall.
The sound bounced from wall to wall. Dust drifted from the roof.
At last the door shuddered and opened a crack. It was only just wide enough.
"That was loud," whispered Ren. "I think the door was asking for a softer voice."
Everyone was shaky but safe, still catching their breath by the horn.

choices.label: Walk on
Look at the horn you just blew

passages.title: The Cracked Horn
paragraphs: Hollis looked at the horn he had just blown.
A thin crack ran along one side of the old bronze.
"Oops," said Hollis. "I did not mean to blow that hard."
Sami sighed, but there was no time to mend it now.
"Maybe we push our luck too far," said Hollis.

choices.label: Walk on
Decide not to push your luck further

passages.title: A Quiet Moment
paragraphs: The team stopped in a small nook. Ren checked the notes. Two chambers were left.
The air felt heavy. Far ahead, a faint light glowed in the dark.
"We can go on," said Sami. "Or we can rest and come back with more help. Both are wise."
Hollis passed round some warm tea from his flask. It tasted of smoke and honey.

choices.label: Go on to the fourth chamber
Leave for today and come back with a bigger team

passages.title: The Hall of Lamps
paragraphs: The fourth chamber was lined with stone lamps. Each one held a pool of old oil.
A Keeper was carved here, holding a tiny flame in its palm.
Under it, one picture showed a huge fire. The picture was crossed out.
Sami lifted a lamp and sniffed. "Keep the flame small," said Sami. "A big fire could burn old things."

choices.label: Light one small lamp, as the Keeper shows
Light a big torch to see better

passages.title: A Small Flame
paragraphs: Ren lit one lamp with a spark. A warm gold light spread across the floor.
It was enough to see a narrow passage ahead. No smoke rose at all.
"Less is more," said Sami. Hollis said he was going to put that on a mug.
The last door stood open. A smooth stone box lay beyond it.

choices.label: Step into the last chamber
Look at the carving once more by the warm light

passages.title: By Golden Light
paragraphs: By the lamp's gold light, Ren saw the Keeper's palm more clearly.
Tiny carved flames circled its fingers, small and neat.
"A careful flame, just like ours," said Ren, smiling.
Ren looked at the last door. "We could wait and come back fresh," said Ren.

choices.label: Step into the last chamber
Decide to wait and come back fresh

passages.title: Too Much Fire
paragraphs: Hollis lit a big torch. Flames leaped. Smoke curled over the lamps.
A black mark crept up the wall. Sami snatched the torch and dipped it in the sand.
"We could burn this room," said Sami. "Old paint does not grow back."
The smoke thinned. The wall had a small scorch, but nothing more.
Everyone was quiet, still standing near the scorch mark on the wall.

choices.label: Step into the last chamber
Check the scorch mark before leaving

passages.title: The Scorch Mark
paragraphs: Sami looked closely at the black mark on the wall.
It was small, but it would never fade away.
"That is the cost of being too quick," said Sami.
Ren wrote it down so no one would forget.
Sami looked tired. "Maybe today has given us enough surprises," said Sami.

choices.label: Step into the last chamber
Decide today has given you enough surprises

passages.title: The Sleeper
paragraphs: The last chamber was still and cool. In its centre lay a big stone box.
A mummified sleeper rested inside. That means a body wrapped in cloth long ago.
The carved Keeper on the wall pointed to the box, then held up a flat hand. A line of tiny pictures ran below.
Nobody spoke. The lamp light shook on the stone lid.
What should the team do?

choices.label: Brush the lid softly and read what is carved there
choices.lockedHint: You need the soft brush and the note from the water wall.

choices.label: Read the pictures on the wall first
Lift the lid just a little to look

passages.title: The Last Warning
paragraphs: Ren read the pictures from left to right. First came the walker, then the cistern, then the singer.
Next came the lamp. Last came the box with a hand over it.
"The Keeper put the chambers in order," said Ren. "Each one teaches a kind of care."
"Sand teaches soft steps. Water teaches looking. Song teaches listening. Fire teaches small flames."
Sami nodded. "So the box teaches us to leave a sleeper at rest."

choices.label: Draw and write everything, and leave the lid shut
Seal the door and tell the city leaders

passages.title: The Keeper Speaks
paragraphs: Sami brushed the lid with slow strokes. Fine dust fell away like flour.
Under it lay a carved line, plain and clear: Rest well. Guard well. Friends may visit, never wake.
Ren read it out. Then Ren hummed the low note, and the whole room hummed back.
Nothing stirred. The lid stayed shut and the sleeper rested on.
"The Keeper was never a warning," said Sami. "It was a welcome, with rules."
The team walked out into the bright day. The tomb was safe, and they knew why.

passages.title: The Open Lid
paragraphs: Hollis and Sami lifted the lid a finger wide. A puff of old air slipped out.
A long, low sound sighed through the room, like wind in a pipe. The lamp went out.
Nobody was hurt. But the room felt sad, as if it had been poked awake.
"We should have read the wall," said Sami softly. They set the lid back and tapped it shut.
They left the tomb that day and told no one for a long time. The sleeper rested again.
Another day, they might read first, and ask later.

passages.title: Every Line Counted
paragraphs: The team worked all afternoon. Ren drew the five chambers, one by one.
Sami dusted each carving once and tapped nothing. Hollis made tea and told only two bad jokes.
By dark they had a map, a song and a hundred notes. The box stayed shut.
Back at camp, Ren read it all aloud by the fire. Hollis filled the tank for the ride home.
Next spring, school children would read it too. The sleeper would never be bothered.

passages.title: The Door Sealed Again
paragraphs: Sami eased the door shut and tapped it closed, slow and careful. The stone sank back into place.
In town, the team told the city leaders what they had found. A guard was set to watch the hill.
It took a whole year to plan the next visit. Ren drew a new map for the people who would come.
Hollis said the wait was long, but the tomb was worth it.
It was not a big finish, but it was a kind one. The sleeper stayed at rest.

passages.title: Another Day
paragraphs: The team packed up carefully and started back toward camp.
Soon they reached the cart, parked past a dry bank of sand.
"We got far today," said Sami. "We have good notes, and that matters."
Hollis told a joke. This time, Ren laughed.
Tomorrow, with fresh eyes, they could try again, and take a different path.

passages.title: Enough For Today
paragraphs: Ren tucked the notebook under one arm. The copied picture would keep until tomorrow.
"Good notes do not need to be rushed," said Sami. "We have come far enough for one day."
Hollis hummed a long, low tune as he waited by the cart.
"Tomorrow, with the card copied twice, we can tap on the sealed door together," said Ren.
For now, the tomb could keep its secrets a little longer.

archaeologist.definition: A person who learns about the past by studying old places and objects.

ancient.definition: Very, very old, from a time long ago.

mummified.definition: Wrapped in cloth and kept safe for a very long time.

cistern.definition: A deep stone tank built to hold water.
